images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A single ivory purchase-order form, crisp and folded once, lies on a small matte graphite tray at the front of a pale neutral tabletop. Along its lower edge sit three empty signature boxes drawn as plain rectangles, with no writing anywhere. Behind it, three more graphite trays stand in a short neat row on slim posts, stepping back toward the rear like stations on a route, each with brushed sides and small hex bolts. The acid-lime element is a narrow ribbon bookmark tucked under the form on the first tray, marking where it must return once signed. A cold frosted glass mug stands beside the last tray. Fine paper fibres and a trace of dust mark the table. The relay route is short and clear. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama, captured mid-disaster. The same first tray, but the relay has sprawled. Dozens of extra graphite trays now stand across the tabletop on posts of different heights, stacked, angled and branching off in every direction like a spreading rail network. Copies of the form sit on many of them, each carrying more rows of empty signature boxes than the last. One sheet is frozen mid-pass between two distant trays, curling in the air, and several are sliding off the far trays and over the table edge. A tray near the back has tipped, dropping a fan of forms. The acid-lime ribbon still lies on the original first tray, which stays empty. Dust hangs over the network, and every branch radiates out from that first tray. Wide 16:9 landscape frame, same layout and angle as the calm version of this scene. The hero object stays slightly left of centre, and the spread of the disaster runs to the right and toward the camera so its path can be traced back to the source. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Photorealistic photograph of a vast handcrafted miniature landscape diorama. A long dry riverbed of cracked pale mud winds across a flat steppe toward a far, hazy horizon. Along both banks stand ruined graphite trays the size of small stations, on toppled or leaning posts, rusted and pitted, forming a broken relay route that meanders out of sight. The riverbed is littered with weathered ivory forms, softened and curled, banked in shallow drifts against stones and snagged in dry grass. In the foreground, the original first tray sits cracked and half buried, its surface dusty. A slim graphite shuttle rig running on a single thin monorail is carrying one recovered form in an acid-lime clasp, heading straight back down the route toward that first tray, its rail laid neatly over the mud. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface.
